{{short description|Online resource for digital poetry}}
The '''Electronic Poetry Center''' ('''EPC'''), is an online resource for [[digital poetry]].  It was founded on July 10, 1994 by [[Loss Pequeño Glazier]] and [[Charles Bernstein (poet)|Charles Bernstein]], of the Poetics Program at [[University at Buffalo|The State University of New York at Buffalo]], making it one of the oldest resources for poetry on the World Wide Web.<ref>Glazier, Loss Peque&ntildeo Glazier, [http://writing.upenn.edu/epc/poetics/archive/logs/txt/1994_07.txt "Announcement: Electronic Poetry Center (Buffalo)"] (''UB Poetics discussion group'', July 10, 1994)</ref>  It was the sponsor of E-Poetry 2001, the world's first festival exclusively dedicated to [[digital poetry|electronic poetry]], which celebrated its tenth anniversary in 2011. The EPC was called "an epicenter of poetic evolution and teaching"<ref>Roseman, Tori, [http://www.ubspectrum.com/news/view.php/846351/Twenty-years-of-living-poetry-Electronic "Twenty years of living poetry: Electronic Poetry Center celebrates decades at the forefront of poetics with EPC@20"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141005143733/http://www.ubspectrum.com/news/view.php/846351/Twenty-years-of-living-poetry-Electronic |date=2014-10-05 }} (''The Spectrum'', Sept. 11, 2014)</ref> as it celebrated its twentieth anniversary, "EPC@20", a two day in festival in Buffalo, September 2014.

In addition to its focus on [[digital poetry]], it also is dedicated to the promotion and archiving of other "contemporary formally innovative poetries."<ref>[http://writing.upenn.edu/epc/about/ Electronic Poetry Center – Introduction<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref>  This is a reflection of its origins in SUNY Buffalo's Poetics Program, a program founded in 1991 by [[Charles Bernstein (poet)|Charles Bernstein]] and [[Robert Creeley]], which maintains a long-standing interest in experimental, progressive, and avant-garde poetics. Glazier was a professor at Buffalo's Department of Media Study.

The extensive curated archives at the site make it a popular destination for the study and enjoyment of contemporary poetry: a 2000 estimate has the site receiving 10 million visits a year.<ref>Ingalls, Zoe, [http://chronicle.com/free/v46/i47/47a05301.htm "A Web Site Grows New Poems, Sometimes Right Before Readers' Eyes."] (''The Chronicle of Higher Education'', July 28, 2000)</ref>

It is partnered with similar organizations, including [[UbuWeb]] and the [[University of Pennsylvania]]'s [[PennSound]] project.
